name: Reverse Structure
description: Play the arrangement in reverse — what was the intro becomes the outro, the build becomes a deconstruction.
usefulWhen: Creating a palindrome-like piece, or the current arrangement feels too predictable in its direction
repair: Not every element should reverse. Keep the harmonic foundation (drone/bass) moving forward while reversing the textural layers for a more subtle effect.
strudelHints: Reverse the order of layer entry/exit
Invert the energy curve: start at peak density and gradually strip layers away

name: Break Tease
description: Preview a section before it arrives — play tiny fragments of what's coming, heavily filtered and quiet. The listener anticipates the full section.
usefulWhen: Building anticipation, creating a sense of something approaching
repair: Keep teases very short (1-2 hits) and sparse (every 4-8 cycles). Too many teases destroy the anticipation.
strudelHints: Play the upcoming layer at .gain(0.1).lpf(500).sometimesBy(0.2, gain(0.3))
Use a single hit from the upcoming pattern as a 'pre-echo'

name: False Drop
description: Build tension and expectation, then pull everything back instead of delivering. The anticlimax becomes more powerful than the climax would have been.
usefulWhen: Subverting expectations, creating memorable structural moments, avoiding predictable builds
repair: Use only once per piece. The first false drop is surprising; the second is annoying. Leave enough space after the fake-out for the real climax later.
strudelHints: Build all layers over 4 cycles, then mute everything except drone on the 'drop' cycle
Roll off high frequencies while building — the release reveals that nothing was actually building at all

name: Asymmetry Injection
description: Break symmetrical phrase lengths by introducing odd-length sections. Instead of 4+4+4+4, try 3+5+7+3.
usefulWhen: The structure feels too predictable, too 'grid-like'
repair: Keep one element (usually the drone or harmonic foundation) at a constant length as an anchor. The asymmetry should feel intentional, not like a mistake.
strudelHints: Use struct() with patterns of different lengths
Add/remove layers on non-standard cycle numbers (3, 5, 7, 11, 13)

name: Subtraction Architecture
description: Instead of adding elements to build intensity, remove them. Strip the pattern down to its essence. What remains becomes more powerful through absence.
usefulWhen: Creating contrast after a dense section, revealing the skeletal structure, creating tension through absence
repair: Keep at least 2 elements in the stripped version so it doesn't become silence. The stripped pattern should still be musically coherent.
strudelHints: Remove layers in order: noise → hi percussion → mid percussion → synth → leave only kick + drone
Increase reverb on remaining elements to fill the space left by removed layers

name: Micro-Variation Architecture
description: Keep the macro-structure constant while introducing tiny changes every cycle. The piece appears static on the surface but is constantly shifting in detail.
usefulWhen: Loop-based music that needs to stay interesting over long durations
repair: Don't vary the core elements (kick, primary rhythm). Only vary secondary elements (percussion details, filter settings, noise layers).
strudelHints: Rotate which secondary elements are active

name: Silence Sculpting
description: Use silence (or near-silence) as a structural element. Strategic gaps of 1-4 cycles where most or all elements drop out.
usefulWhen: Creating dramatic tension, marking structural boundaries, giving the listener a moment of reflection
repair: Keep one element (very quiet drone or reverb tail) during the silence so it doesn't feel like the music stopped. Pure digital silence is jarring.
strudelHints: Mute all layers except a very quiet drone for 2-4 cycles
Keep the reverb tail of the last hit as the only sound during the gap

name: Accumulation Pattern
description: Start with a single element. Add one new element every N cycles. Each addition transforms the character of the whole. The piece 'grows' rather than 'changes'.
usefulWhen: Opening a piece, building toward a dense section, creating a sense of organic growth
repair: Space additions at least 4 cycles apart. Each new layer should be introduced at low gain and gradually brought up over 2-4 cycles.
strudelHints: Add layers at intervals with .gain('<0 0.5 1>').slow(4) fade-in
Order: drone → bass → texture → percussion → detail → full density
